newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products firm except for easier light ends.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products firm except for easier light ends.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Monday.

Gasoline was weaker as NYMEX unleaded fell back. An Italian player bought a 25,000 tonne premium leaded Saras-quality cargo, loading in mid September, from an Italian refiner. The deal was done at a $1.50 premium to the quoted fob high, fob Med.
The same buyer was heard having bought a Eurograde cargo on Friday from Italy, but the price was not known.
Naphtha was also weaker with crude. Offers of Ras Lanuf barrels were seen, and Russian full-range cargoes were seen emerging for later in the month.
Gas oil was firm with talk on low sulphur material dominating the market ahead of the introduction of EU 0.05 percent sulphur regulations on October 1.
There were unconfirmed rumours a 0.05 percent cargo had traded at Oct IPE +$19 basis Genoa.
At least three large cargoes of Canadian low sulphur diesel were reported to be headed for the Med as traders took advantage of the arbitrage created by current high premiums on low sulphur material.
Two Russian cargoes were on offer with premiums assessed at quotes cif high +$2/+$3 basis Genoa.
High sulphur cracked fuel oil remains scarce, particularly good quality bunker spec, and prices were seen about +$2/3 above Med quotes.

An Isab cargo was understood to be available at the end of the month at a price, traders said, that would be close to +1/1.50 on the quote. Some bunker requirement into Italy was still uncovered and this was expected to initiate active buying which traders thought would strengthen the quality premium.
The low sulphur market was a reluctant follower of crude's recent rally, but swaps numbers of $111.50 for Sept indicated further price gains on the physical side. -- +44 171 542 8980
